headline: Methods separate coordinated gene programs from confounding variation in transcriptomes
label: Single Cell Spatial Transcriptomics Methods
summary: Multi-slice spatial atlases and lineage-barcoded single-cell data now demand models that separate biological structure from patient and technical variation.
synthesis: The dominant thread is separating coordinated biological structure from confounding variation in transcriptomic data. DeSPA uses linear mixed models to detect cross-state spatial pattern remodeling across multi-slice atlases, and SORT applies matrix factorization with orthogonality and graph total variation to recover multilevel spatial gene programs across patients. These two items most directly pair multi-slice spatial organization with cross-state or cross-patient comparison. ALBIS contributes a simulator that generates multi-resolution 2D sections from 3D tissues with ground truth, which supports evaluation of such methods. Other items address distinct problems: DKO predicts cell-specific virtual perturbation effects and reports rising heterogeneity with aging, IsoGraph separates isoform usage from gene abundance in the aging human brain, PRISM estimates sample-specific correlation networks, and BEAST and FateScape use lineage barcodes for phylogenetic and division-history inference.
